transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been carrying this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger since my friend was killed. I thought it would ease with time, but it hasn’t.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, distressing memories or images of what happened popping into your mind?

Yes. A crosswalk signal, the sound of a truck, even seeing one of those walking-tour maps can bring it all back at once. I see my friend stepping off the curb so clearly—it just pops into my head before I can stop it.
About how long ago did this happen to your friend?
It was about two years and three months ago, on that walking tour.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid places, sounds, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yes. I take a different route so I don’t have to go near that intersection. And I’ve stopped signing up for most tours or safety meetings—the conversation always seems to circle back to what happened, and I just can’t bear it.
Do you often feel constantly on guard, jumpy, or easily startled?
Yes. Near traffic, I’m watching every truck, every curb, every person crossing. It feels like I have to spot something dangerous before it happens again.

patient.answer: Yes. A crosswalk signal, the sound of a truck, even seeing one of those walking-tour maps can bring it all back at once. I see my friend stepping off the curb so clearly—it just pops into my head before I can stop it.

inference.note: Patient confirms intrusive trauma re-experiencing triggered by environmental cues; removed F41.1 and F43.8 as symptoms clearly point to trauma- and stressor-related disorders, added F43.0 pending duration clarification.

doctor.intent: Determine the time elapsed since the traumatic event to differentiate acute stress reaction from PTSD
doctor.question: About how long ago did this happen to your friend?

target_item.name: Duration

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long ago the traumatic event occurred.

patient.answer: It was about two years and three months ago, on that walking tour.

inference.note: Ruled out F43.0 (acute stress reaction) because the traumatic event occurred over two years ago.

doctor.intent: Assess for persistent avoidance of trauma-related reminders
doctor.question: Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid places, sounds, or activities that remind you of what happened?

target_item.name: Trauma_Avoidance

patient.answer: Yes. I take a different route so I don’t have to go near that intersection. And I’ve stopped signing up for most tours or safety meetings—the conversation always seems to circle back to what happened, and I just can’t bear it.

inference.note: Ruled out F43.2 due to the severe traumatic nature of the stressor, duration exceeding two years, and prominent re-experiencing and avoidance symptoms characteristic of PTSD.

doctor.intent: Assess for symptoms of hyperarousal such as hypervigilance or feeling constantly on edge
doctor.question: Do you often feel constantly on guard, jumpy, or easily startled?

target_item.name: Hypervigilance
target_item.manifestation: Whenever I am near traffic, I watch every truck, curb, and pedestrian like it is my responsibility to catch danger before it happens again.
target_item.reason: The question most directly asks about being constantly on guard and easily startled, which reflects hypervigilance.

patient.answer: Yes. Near traffic, I’m watching every truck, every curb, every person crossing. It feels like I have to spot something dangerous before it happens again.

inference.note: Hypervigilance and persistent threat monitoring confirmed, fulfilling all core criteria for PTSD (F43.1) and ruling out primary depressive episode (F32).
